Log in to check out faster. Continue shopping ABOUT US We are a fashion multi designer store that believes in bringing timeless, elegant pieces that empower individuals to express their unique style. Our commitment to quality, sustainability, and customer satisfaction drives everything we do. OUR STORY Two journeys, one table, and a cup of tea that changed everything. After walking our own paths and experiencing different chapters of life, we finally sat down one evening and asked ourselves—what if we build something together? What started as simple conversations over endless cups of tea slowly turned into ideas, and those ideas grew into a shared belief. We didn’t know how far we would go, but we knew we wanted to create something bigger than where we came from. That belief became Trovelle—an online marketplace for designer wear clothing, built with the vision of bringing beautiful, thoughtfully designed fashion from talented designers to people who truly appreciate it. And this is just the beginning of our journey. as2hrk2xrc2zlwvvzstwocolumnblock1 RUPAL GUPTA I’ve always been someone who chooses the best in life and constantly pushes myself to grow. For the past 10 years, I built my career as an Engineering Manager, leading teams, solving complex problems, and thriving in the corporate world. I was a full-on corporate slay… until the day my company suddenly shut down. In that moment, everything paused, and I found myself standing at a crossroad—play it safe or take a leap of faith. I chose the scarier path: to believe in myself and build something bigger than just a job title, something louder than my fears. That’s the reason I created this marketplace—to turn uncertainty into opportunity and build something meaningful of my own. CHAVI KANSAL I’ve always been a young, optimistic girl who believes life is full of opportunities waiting to be explored. In my early years, I was a corporate girlie—driven by targets, meetings, and big ambitions. Then life evolved, and I stepped into new roles as a homemaker and the proud mother of a beautiful daughter. While these roles shaped me in many ways, one dream always stayed constant—the desire to create something meaningful, something I could nurture and grow every single day. Not just a business, but a beginning I chose for myself. And that’s exactly why I started this marketplace—this is the start of my entrepreneurial journey. Blending timeless elegance with contemporary sensibility, Manju Tomar creates heirloom-worthy pieces for women who value beauty with intention — where every silhouette carries a story, soul, and enduring legacy. Shopping for a high-end Indian wedding outfit online is not simply a matter of finding the right lehenga. It's about finding a platform you can trust one that authenticates its designers, curates thoughtfully, and understands the difference between festive and bridal. Multi-designer stores solve this problem by bringing dozens (sometimes hundreds) of verified labels under a single roof. Three platforms consistently rise to the top of that list. Here's how they compare, and how to pick the right one for your occasion. Why is Aza Fashion the top choice for high-end multi-designer Indian wedding shopping? Aza Fashion positions itself as a premium, editorially curated platform and it earns that label. The site stocks over 200 verified designer brands, including Anita Dongre, Rohit Bal, Shantanu & Nikhil, and Rimple & Harpreet Narula. Every label is vetted before joining the platform, which removes the guesswork that comes with browsing less curated marketplaces. The catalogue spans lehengas, sarees, anarkalis, sharara sets, and gowns covering everything from the bride herself to wedding guests across multiple functions. Aza Fashion also holds a 4.4/5 rating on Trustpilot across 5,000+ reviews, reflecting consistent satisfaction among shoppers. The weeks leading up to Diwali bring a flurry of decisions: which outfit for the puja, which look for the party, which colour this year. This guide covers everything you need to put together the perfect Diwali ethnic wear looks for 2026. What to Wear for Diwali: The Basics Colour matters. Traditional Diwali colours include deep reds, royal blues, emerald greens, mustard yellows, and gold. Fabric sets the occasion. Puja calls for something graceful and traditional; the evening party invites more drama and shine. Comfort is non-negotiable. You will be sitting, standing, lighting diyas, eating, so your outfit needs to move with you. Diwali Outfit Ideas for 2026 1. The Embroidered Suit Set A classic for a reason. An embroidered suit set in jewel tones, deep wine, midnight blue, or emerald green, hits the sweet spot between traditional and refined. Pair with statement jhumkas and a potli bag. Shop our Festive Wear collection . 2. The Farshi Salwar Set The farshi salwar's floor-sweeping hem creates instant drama without requiring heavy embellishment. Opt for an ombre farshi in dusty rose or burnt orange for a modern Diwali look that photographs beautifully. 3. The Co-Ord Set in Festive Colours For Diwali parties and friends' gatherings, a festive co-ord set in rich brocade or printed fabric is effortlessly chic. Browse Co-Ord Sets . 4. The Cape Set A cape jacket set layered over a matching kurta and pant is the Diwali party outfit of the moment. The cape adds drama, the co-ordinated base keeps it grounded. 5. The Kaani Suit Set For those who want something deeply rooted in Indian craft traditions, a Kaani jacquard suit set is unmatched. Shop Kaani Suit Sets . Shop Our Diwali Bestsellers Black Shirt with Brocade Pants Shop Now Navy Blue Crush Suit with Chanderi Dupatta Shop Now Wine Velvet Suit with Tulip Pants Shop Now Diwali Outfit Colours to Watch in 2026 Burgundy and wine: Rich, traditional, always right for Diwali Forest green and emerald: Fresh and festive, pairs beautifully with gold jewellery Dusty rose and blush: Soft and elegant for day events and puja Ivory and cream: Understated luxury, especially beautiful in embroidered fabrics Midnight blue: A modern alternative to black for evening Diwali parties Diwali Jewellery and Styling Tips Chandelier earrings or jhumkas work with almost every ethnic silhouette A potli bag in coordinating fabric elevates any outfit Keep your dupatta draped loosely for comfort, or opt for a set that does not require one Block heels or juttis are more practical and just as stylish as stilettos for a long Diwali evening Shop our full Diwali Festive Collection and find your perfect Diwali look. While traditional wear is always a beautiful choice, there’s a fresh trend on the rise— Indo-Western outfits . These striking ensembles perfectly blend Eastern elegance and Western chic, giving you the best of both worlds. Gone are the days when Diwali meant sticking to only traditional lehengas or sarees. Today’s fashion scene allows you to experiment, combine, and redefine festive wear. So, why not step out of your comfort zone this Diwali and explore the world of Indo-Western outfits for women ? Whether attending a family puja, hosting a Diwali dinner, or partying with friends, there’s an Indo-Western look for every occasion. Here are 10 stunning Indo-Western outfit ideas that will ensure you sparkle and stand out this Diwali. Let’s dive right into it! 1. The Fiery Red Co-Ord Set – Effortless Elegance with a Dash of Festivity First on the list is a vibrant red co-ord set that perfectly blends elegance with modern style. Co-ord sets have become immensely popular for their easy-to-wear yet fashionable appeal. This ensemble features a matching top and wide-legged trousers, offering comfort and sophistication. The beauty of this Indo-Western outfit lies in its simplicity. The tailored cut of the trousers balances the flowy top, creating a streamlined, effortlessly chic look. Perfect for Diwali parties or family gatherings, the bright red hue immediately adds a festive flair, while the minimalistic design ensures you remain comfortable throughout the night. Styling Tip : Pair this ethnic co-ord set with statement earrings and sleek heels for a modern, polished look. Want to amp up the Diwali vibe? Add a bold red lipstick to complete your stunning ensemble. 2. The Glamorous Wine Corset Set – A Fusion of Structure and Flow Looking for something that has the wow factor? Enter the Wine corset set , a luxurious Indo-Western outfit for Diwali that combines the best of both worlds—Western corsetry and traditional Indian silhouettes. The fitted corset-style bodice beautifully complements the flowing skirt, creating a glamorous yet refined look perfect for evening events. Corset-inspired outfits have been dominating the designer Indo-Western outfit scene, and for a good reason—they highlight your figure while adding an element of drama to your ensemble. This deep burgundy piece is ideal for women who want to step out in something unique yet festive. Styling Tip : With this outfit, keep accessories minimal since the corset adds plenty of detail. Opt for soft waves or a sleek bun, and let the rich colour and structure of the outfit speak for itself. 3. The Classic Sharara Set – Timeless Festive Glam No Diwali wardrobe is complete without a fabulous sharara set , and this red embroidered sharara set is as festive as possible. Sharara sets have been integral to Indian festive wear for centuries, but today’s designers have given them a contemporary twist. The wide-legged pants and an intricately embroidered kurta make this sharara set for women a must-have for the festive season. The standout feature of this outfit is its detailed embroidery, which adds a touch of grandeur without going overboard. The sharara’s flared pants allow for easy movement, whether you’re dancing at a Diwali party or performing a traditional puja. Styling Tip : To complete the festive look, pair this outfit with bold gold jewellery and strappy sandals. The dhoti kurta set for women is a bold choice that will turn heads this Diwali. This look combines the relaxed comfort of the dhoti with the structured elegance of a fitted kurta. The result? Show off an embroidered neckline with a single-shoulder drape, let a decorative dupatta frame a simpler kurta, and secure loose fabric when you need your hands free. Then choose jewellery and shoes around the occasion, rather than adding everything at once. A different drape can change the mood of the same suit. The trick is choosing one that looks good and stays comfortable while you sit, greet people or dance. Start with the neckline, fabric and silhouette Before reaching for accessories, put on the full set and look at where the detail sits. If the neckline is heavily embroidered, avoid hiding it beneath several layers of fabric. If the kurta is understated but the dupatta has a beautiful border, give that border room to show. Volume matters too. Wide sharara trousers already bring movement to an outfit, so a neatly arranged dupatta can balance the look. A straighter suit leaves more room for a fuller drape. These are useful starting points, not rules about what you can wear. Three dupatta drapes to try The single-shoulder drape Arrange the dupatta over one shoulder, either in soft folds or loose pleats, with the border facing out. Adjust the front and back lengths so neither end catches under your shoes. This leaves the kurta neckline visible and works well when you want the embroidery to lead. Try this with the Naaz Blush Pink Hand Embroidered Sharara Set . Its contrast pink organza dupatta adds a distinct layer against the blush kurta and crushed-tissue trousers. The open, two-shoulder drape Rest the dupatta across both shoulders, leaving the front open enough to show the kurta. It gives the outfit a softly framed look and displays a decorative border without tightly wrapping the fabric. Check the drape while seated as well as standing. A wide spread can look lovely in photographs but may slip when you lean forward. If it needs constant attention, narrow the folds or choose a more secure arrangement. The pleated, secured drape For a sangeet or a busy family gathering, make soft pleats and secure the dupatta at the shoulder with a suitable garment pin. Keep the ends clear of your hands and feet. Test any fastening carefully so it does not snag delicate tissue or organza. A belt can work with some suits, but it is optional. Avoid forcing a bulky or heavily embroidered dupatta beneath a tight belt, and make sure you can sit comfortably before committing to the look. How to style your suit for different celebrations Daytime wedding functions Keep the outfit manageable for the venue and weather. Earrings, comfortable footwear and a secure dupatta may be all you need. If you are having mehendi applied, arrange the fabric away from your hands before the appointment. The Ziya Ivory Tissue Embroidered Sharara Set offers a lighter palette with a contrasting embroidered neckline and coordinated borders. Keep additional accessories restrained if you want those details to stand out. Sangeet and reception evenings Let either the outfit or the jewellery take the lead. An embroidered neckline often needs little more than earrings; a simpler neckline can leave room for a statement necklace. Choose shoes you have already walked in, especially if the evening includes dancing. For cooler-weather celebrations, consider the Bottle Green Crush Velvet Embroidered Sharara Set . Its velvet suit and organza dupatta offer contrasting textures. Check the venue temperature and lining details rather than assuming velvet will suit every evening event. Diwali and family festivals A familiar suit can feel different with a new drape, a different pair of earrings or a change of footwear. You do not need a completely new outfit for every invitation. If celebrations involve lamps or candles, keep loose dupatta ends well away from flames. For more event-specific inspiration, read our Diwali dressing guide . Pair jewellery and accessories without overcrowding the look Repeat one detail rather than matching everything. You might pick up the embroidery's metallic tone in your earrings, or echo a dupatta colour in a small bag. Exact colour matching is optional. Try the complete outfit before deciding on a necklace. A piece that looks lovely on its own may compete with an ornate neckline. Equally, a plain kurta can be a good backdrop for jewellery you want to showcase. Share Prev Next October 27, 2026 Sharara vs Farshi Salwar: What’s the Difference? A sharara has two wide, flared trouser legs. A farshi salwar is a generous salwar silhouette known for its long, floor-reaching drape. A gharara is usually fitted through the upper leg, with a distinct joint near the knee and a fuller flare below. That knee joint is the detail most often confused with a sharara. If you have been using the names interchangeably, you are not alone. Contemporary labels sometimes overlap, so look at the cut, hem and product photographs rather than relying on the name alone. Sharara, farshi salwar and gharara at a glance Style Defining detail Overall effect Sharara Wide, flared legs, generally without a pronounced fitted knee joint A flowing, trouser-like silhouette with plenty of movement Farshi salwar A roomy salwar cut with extra length and a floor-reaching drape A generous, trailing silhouette Gharara A fitted upper leg joined to a flared lower section near the knee A defined change in volume below the knee What is a farshi salwar? The word farshi is associated with the floor, which gives a useful clue to the garment's defining feature: length and drape. A farshi salwar carries generous fabric through a loose salwar silhouette, with a hem that reaches or trails along the floor. It is not simply another name for wide-leg trousers. The salwar construction and the way the fabric gathers and falls are part of its character. Modern versions vary, so check the actual measurements and photographs before choosing one. What is a sharara? A sharara is a pair of wide-legged, flared trousers, often worn with a kurta or tunic and a dupatta. The legs can create an almost skirt-like effect in motion, but they remain separate trouser legs. A fitted thigh and a sharply defined knee joint are not essential sharara features. Those details are more characteristic of a gharara. Sharara designs can still vary in their panels, gathers and amount of flare. How is a gharara different? Look for the join around the knee. A gharara is generally more fitted above this point, with a wider lower section attached below it. The join may be highlighted with embroidery or decorative trim. Neither a sharara nor a gharara is automatically heavier, more formal or more comfortable than the other. Fabric, lining, embroidery and fit make a bigger difference to how an outfit feels. How to choose your outfit for a celebration For a mehendi or sangeet Start with movement. Try sitting, walking and taking a few dance steps in the outfit, with the shoes you plan to wear. A sharara can give you a lovely sweep without a trailing hem, provided the length is right. For a traditional wedding function Choose the silhouette you enjoy wearing. A gharara gives a more defined knee flare, while a farshi salwar brings a long, generous drape. Neither needs to be reserved for a particular body type. For a winter evening Consider the fabric as carefully as the silhouette. Velvet may suit cooler evenings, while lighter fabrics can feel easier at warm indoor venues. Check the lining, sleeve length and layering options rather than assuming any particular cut will keep you warm. Does INCHING INDIA have sharara sets? Yes. A floral suit, an embroidered co-ord or a softly coloured kurta set can bring that balance without needing a heavily layered look. Start with your family's plans and dress expectations. Are you staying for lunch, visiting more than one home or changing for an evening gathering? Choose the silhouette around the day you will actually have, then add a little jewellery and footwear you can comfortably wear throughout it. A floral suit for a family Bhai Dooj celebration A kurta-and-salwar combination is an easy starting point for an ethnic look. Printed borders add detail without requiring several accessories, and matching pieces keep the outfit feeling considered. The Green Printed Salwar Set combines a lime green base with floral borders. Its product specifications list cotton linen. Try small earrings and comfortable flats, letting the print provide the festive colour. If you prefer a dupatta with your outfit, choose a coordinating piece you already own and check that the drape feels manageable while sitting and moving. Follow your family's preferences rather than treating one styling choice as a rule for everyone. A printed co-ord for Bhai Dooj lunch A matching co-ord is useful when you want a complete look without spending time pairing separate pieces. Choose a print you would also wear for lunches and visits after the festival, so the outfit has a place in your everyday wardrobe. The cotton-linen Cream Roses Printed Linen Set pairs a cream base with rose motifs and pink borders. Keep the bag plain and choose one accessory, such as earrings or a bracelet, rather than introducing several competing colours. For a softer pink option, consider the Tulip Pink Printed Linen Set , also listed as cotton linen. Check the dimensions and composition before choosing the fit for your plans. An embroidered lilac suit for a dressed-up gathering If you prefer texture to print, embroidery can give a simple silhouette enough detail for the occasion. Soft lilac offers colour without the intensity of a deep purple outfit. The cotton Lilac Embroidered Suit Set features white cutwork detailing on the kurta and matching pants. Small earrings and a simple bag keep the focus on the embroidery. Add a layer only if the weather and venue call for one. A relaxed co-ord for a quieter celebration A festive outfit does not have to be elaborate. For a small gathering at home, the cotton Pink Co-Ord Set offers a softer option with a floral motif and lace detailing. Style it with a favourite pair of earrings and familiar sandals. A piece of jewellery with a personal connection can make the look feel more like you than adding accessories simply because it is a festival. How to accessorise your Bhai Dooj outfit Let either the clothing or the jewellery take the lead. With a busy floral print, try restrained accessories. With a simpler outfit, a statement pair of earrings can provide the finishing touch without needing a necklace as well. You can choose a Farshi salwar that expresses your personal style with the aid of these tips. What is a Farshi salwar? A Farshi salwar's wide, flowing drape is a defining feature of this kind of generously cut trousers. The name is associated with the word farsh, which means floor, referring to the garment's traditional long sweep. Many styles are completed with a dupatta, and it is usually worn with a kurta. Modern Farshi sets are not required to follow the floor. More recent versions often keep the volume while improving the length's wearability. Look at the measurements and pictures of the actual clothing instead of assuming that every Farshi set will have the same cut. A synopsis of its history The Farshi design is linked to the Indian history courtly fashion traditions. Its sweeping style, ample fabric, and focus on the entire set rather than just the trousers make it appealing. Today's interpretations provide that sense of occasion more manageable shapes. A brocade kurta with soft pants or a lighter kurta with an embroidered hem are both options. Rather than being precise copies of historical apparel, think of these as contemporary adaptations of a classic silhouette. What makes a Farshi salwar different from a sharara or a regular salwar? A typical salwar gathers in the direction of a narrower ankle. A Farshi salwar has a broader, more flowing fall around the feet. A gharara is more likely to have a fitted upper leg with a pronounced flare beginning at the knee, whereas shararas are usually flared, wide-legged trousers. The names are sometimes applied loosely, therefore photographs and structural information are your best option. If you're comparing shapes for a celebration, look at our women's suit sets and Farshi sets . Note where the kurta swells and how much of each trouser is visible beneath it. As a guest, the aim is to look festive, feel comfortable and respect the way the couple and their families are celebrating. You do not need to guess your way through every custom. Start with the invitation and ask when something is unclear. This guide is about wedding guest dress-code etiquette: choosing colours thoughtfully, matching the venue and avoiding an outfit that needs attention all evening. Read the invitation before choosing an outfit Check for a colour theme, dress code or venue note. The invitation or family WhatsApp group may tell you whether a celebration is traditional, relaxed or more formal. Follow those details rather than assuming every Indian wedding has the same expectations. If the instructions are vague, ask the host a specific question, such as whether guests should wear traditional clothing or whether a particular colour is reserved for close family. It is easier to check before shopping than to worry about it on the day. Choose colours with the family’s customs in mind Can a wedding guest wear red? Red is associated with bridal clothing in many communities, but it is not reserved for brides at every wedding. Ask if you are unsure, particularly if your outfit is heavily embellished or looks bridal. A different colour is a simple option when you do not have guidance. What about black and white? Preferences vary by family, region and community. Some hosts welcome either colour; others prefer guests to avoid them at particular ceremonies. The family’s instructions matter more than a general rule found online. This overview of wedding traditions in India offers background on the variety of celebrations, but it is not a substitute for the host’s dress code. Dress for the venue, not just the photograph Beach and garden venues Think about heat, wind and the ground beneath your feet. Long hems can collect sand or trail across damp grass, and narrow heels may be difficult on uneven surfaces. Choose shoes and a drape you can manage comfortably. Indoor and formal venues A more polished silhouette can suit a formal setting, but comfort still matters. Check that you can sit through the ceremony and move easily between spaces. If the venue has strong air conditioning, a shawl may be useful. Religious ceremonies Ask whether the ceremony or venue has specific requirements for clothing, head coverings or footwear. Carrying a dupatta or shawl can be helpful when requested, but do not assume the same practice applies everywhere. Look festive without dressing like the bride There is room for embroidery, jewellery and rich colours in a guest outfit. The question is how they work together. If your clothing already has detailed embroidery, you may prefer simpler jewellery. If the outfit is plain, a statement accessory or bordered dupatta can be enough. Choose a look that suits your relationship to the couple and the dress code. When there is any doubt about an elaborate bridal-style outfit, check with the host rather than trying to work out a universal limit. For a coordinated look, explore our suit sets for women . So instead of answering it forty times individually, here's the whole thing in one place - written the way we'd actually tell a friend, not a search engine. What should women wear on Karwa Chauth? Honestly, red and maroon are still winning, but we're seeing a lot more women pick deep pink and even bottle green with gold zari this year. If you want the classic bridal-adjacent look, a heavily embroidered saree does the job every time. Going for a lehenga instead? Great choice if it's your first Karva Chauth as a married woman and you want photos that look like an event, not just an outfit. Not everyone wants that much weight on them though, especially since you're fasting from sunrise. A well-cut suit set is our quiet recommendation - it looks festive, moves easily, and doesn't need constant adjusting during the pooja. Chikankari or bandhani pieces are the move if you'd rather be comfortable than dramatic. Whatever you land on, a good dupatta pulled over the head for the moon sighting finishes the look properly. There's no wrong answer here, just depends on how your evening is shaping up - a big family gathering versus a quiet one at home. What are traditional Karwa Chauth gifts? Gifting used to be a one-way thing - husband gifts wife - but that's changed a lot. Mothers-in-law gift daughters-in-law, sisters gift each other, friends exchange small things too. The sargi thali is still the heart of the morning: sweets, dry fruits, maybe a few snacks the mother-in-law traditionally sends over. For the evening, bangles and a fresh set of mehendi cones are almost always welcome. If you want to gift something with more weight, jewelry that matches whatever outfit she's already picked works well, or you could just gift the outfit itself and let her build the rest around it - that's usually the gift that gets remembered longest. We put together a Festive Wear collection with exactly this in mind, in case you're shopping last minute (we won't judge, most people are). If you're gifting for someone who prefers understated over heavy work, our Sarees edit has a lot of lighter, everyday-festive options too. A few more things people ask us What colors are considered auspicious for Karwa Chauth? Red, maroon, pink, and gold, mostly because of what they symbolize in Indian tradition - love and a long married life. Green and yellow show up too, just less often. Can I wear something other than a saree? Yes, and plenty of women do. Lehengas, suit sets , even a well-chosen chikankari kurta set are all fine. Wear what you'll actually enjoy fasting in for twelve-plus hours. What's a good last-minute gift if I've completely forgotten? A set of bangles or a small jewelry piece from a nearby store works in a pinch, but if you have even a day, a festive outfit from our Festive Wear range tends to land better and lasts longer than sweets. Looking for more festive inspiration beyond Karwa Chauth? Our Diwali Festive Collection is also worth a browse while you're at it. It is when women dress up traditionally, often in a saree to honor their Indian culture and heritage. The saree you choose to wear should feel intentional, easy to sit in, and beautiful enough to be remembered for years to come. Embroidery is the right choice for Diwali Puja specifically because embroidered sarees carry their own festivity in the fabric itself. The saree does the work. Here are five embroidered sarees from trueBrowns' New Festive collection, each suited to a different kind of Diwali puja, from the intimate home ceremony to the joint-family gathering. trueBrowns Peach Boota Embroidered Georgette Saree As the dusk settles in and courtyards come aglow with the flickering diyas, this peach embroidered saree turns into the most beautiful part of your Diwali evening. This peach georgette saree with boota embroidery and scallop border detailing is warm in color, light in fabric, and radiant in its festivity. Georgette drapes effortlessly and stays comfortable through a long evening of ritual. The contrast maroon unstitched embroidered blouse piece adds depth without drama. Co-ord Set How to Style trueBrowns Viscose Co-ord Sets for the Festive Season Kurta Sets & Co-ord Sets for Ganesh Chaturthi, Durga Puja & Navratri 2026 Indian festive dressing is changing. The new memo: not every festive moment calls for a lehenga. India's festive calendar between August and November 2026 is full of little celebrations — a Ganesh Chaturthi aarti at home, a Durga Puja pandal visit with family, a colleague's Navratri lunch, a neighbor's Diwali gathering. These are real moments that deserve real dressing-up, without the weight and fuss of heavy embellished festive wear. trueBrowns has launched a new edit of solid viscose rayon kurta sets and co-ord sets designed for exactly these moments — lightweight, fluid, and festive in their simplicity. Made from 100% viscose rayon fabric in numerous solid colors, these sets are priced at Rs. 2,499 each and are available in inclusive sizing from XS to 6XL. This guide maps each set to a specific festive occasion across the Indian festive calendar of 2026, so you know exactly which one to reach for and when. Why Viscose Is the Right Fabric for Festive Season Ethnic Wear Viscose is a fabric derived from natural cellulose. It has the softness and drape of silk but is significantly more affordable, easier to care for, and lighter in weight. For festive dressing in India between August and November, viscose has three key advantages over traditional festive fabrics. It drapes like silk: A solid viscose rayon kurta set or co-ord set in a jewel tone reads as occasion-appropriate and polished without requiring dry cleaning or delicate handling. This makes it practical for frequent festive occasions, like multiple pujas, family lunches, or celebrations throughout the season. It stays comfortable in the transition weather: Viscose is lightweight and breathable enough to stay comfortable in this in-between weather, unlike heavier festive fabrics that are designed for cooler temperatures. Solid colors in viscose photograph beautifully: Festive occasions are increasingly documented. Solid viscose co-ord sets in saturated colors like lime, blue, and olive brown photograph with exceptional richness, making them as visually impactful in a photo as they are in person. For the Ganesh Chaturthi Aarti: trueBrowns Lime Solid Viscose Co-ord Set The morning aarti at home, when the whole family gathers, prasad is distributed, and the modaks come out, is one of the most joyful festive moments of Ganesh Chaturthi. It calls for an outfit that is bright and auspicious, comfortable enough to sit on the floor and participate in the ritual, and easy enough to put on without effort on an early morning. The trueBrowns Lime Solid Viscose Co-ord Set answers all three. Lime is a vivid, energetic color that reads as celebratory without the formality of red or the heaviness of gold. The regular-fit top with a round V-neckline and three-fourth sleeves pairs with lime flared pants that have a fully elasticated waist, making it comfortable to wear through a long celebratory morning. A side slit on the top provides ease of movement. Both the top and pants are unlined, keeping the set light and breathable. Two pockets are built into the pants. IKKIVI COLLECTION Your Resort-Ready Capsule Resort trips and warm-weather getaways all ask the same quiet question: what do you actually pack so you're not living out of a suitcase, rewearing the same three things, or carrying clothes that wrinkle the second they come out of your bag? A capsule approach solves it. Instead of packing outfit by outfit, you pack a small set of pieces: breathable fabrics, easy silhouettes, a tight color story. These pieces mix and match into a full week (or two) of looks, whether you're island hopping in the Bahamas, poolside at a resort, or working your way through a warm climate city break. This guide walks you through how to build that capsule, what fabrics actually hold up to travel and heat, and which pieces from IKKIVI's resort and travel edits are built for exactly this kind of trip. They're ethically made, in sizes 2XS to 5XL. Why Linen (and Natural Fibers) Are the Resort-Wear MVP If there's one fabric decision that makes or breaks your warm-weather packing list, it's choosing natural, breathable fibers over synthetics. Linen in particular has become the go-to for resort and travel wardrobes, for a few concrete reasons: It breathes. Linen is a looser weave natural fiber, so air moves through it. It won't trap heat against your skin the way polyester or other synthetics do, which matters directly in humid, tropical climates. It handles heat and humidity well. Linen absorbs moisture and releases it quickly, so it feels drier against your skin in hot, sticky weather than most synthetic blends. The lived-in wrinkle is part of the look. Linen creases naturally. That relaxed, slightly rumpled look is part of its appeal for travel and resort settings, so you don't need to fight it. You can style it down or up easily. The same linen piece works for a beach walk at noon and a dinner reservation at eight, with a swap of shoes and jewelry. You'll find exactly this in IKKIVI's Linen edit : 100% linen tops, trousers, dresses, and sets designed for warm climates, alongside organic cotton and other natural-fiber pieces across the Resort Wear and Travel Easy collections. Build Your Capsule: 5 Pieces That Do the Work You don't need twelve outfits. You need five to seven pieces that combine into twelve. Here's how to think about the categories, with real options you can shop right now. 1. The Linen Co-ord Set (your beach-to-dinner uniform) A matching linen or linen-blend top-and-bottom set is the single most efficient resort packing choice: it reads as a finished outfit on its own, and each piece also works separately with something else in your bag. Zulu Black Linen Pant Set and Zulu Blue Linen Pant Set : shirt-and-trouser linen sets built for exactly this kind of mix-and-match travel styling. Sahara Linen Crop Top & Skirt Set : a lighter, cropped silhouette for daytime heat. You can browse the full range in Co-ord Sets . 2. The One-and-Done Jumpsuit A jumpsuit is the closest thing to packing an outfit instead of a garment. Zero matching is required, and it looks considered the moment you put it on. Pack one in a print and one in a solid, and you've covered most of a week's dinners. Evening Chai Jumpsuit : an easy, relaxed silhouette. Ikat Jumpsuit and Ocean Patch Jumpsuit : pattern-driven pieces that work as your trip's statement outfit. Oceanarium Jumpsuit and Sweet Lavender Jumpsuit : softer colorways for daytime wear. Blue Daisy Day Jumpsuit and Ivory Daisy Day Jumpsuit : lighter prints suited to daytime resort settings. You'll find the complete range in Jumpsuits & Rompers . 3. Breathable Linen Separates (the mix-and-match workhorses) Separates are what actually stretch your capsule. One top can pair with two or three bottoms across a trip. Indigo Splash Linen Shirt paired with its matching Indigo Splash Linen Pants : wear them together or split them across different outfits. The Ghar Linen Trousers and The Neev Linen Trousers : versatile linen trousers you can rotate under multiple tops. The Ghar Linen Peplum Top : a structured top you can dress down with shorts by day and dress up with trousers at night. Ocean Breeze Linen Pants : a lightweight bottom built for warm-climate wear. 4. One Statement Dress for Dinner Every resort capsule earns one dress that's a little more special. Pack light everywhere else so you have room for this one. Golden Palm Linen Dress : a linen maxi dress designed as an easy dinner-ready piece. 5. Color and Print for Vacation Energy Resort wardrobes lean into color in a way your everyday wardrobe doesn't. That color is part of what signals vacation rather than work trip. IKKIVI's Leheriya tie-dye sets are built specifically around this: Candy Leheriya Co-ord Set , Ocean Leheriya Co-ord Set , and Tropical Leheriya Co-ord Set : tie-dye print sets in distinct colorways. Leheriya Blue Co-ord and Sunrise Tie & Dye Co-ord Set : more tie-dye options for a vacation-forward palette. Strappy Hills (Set of 2) and Void Panzo Set : additional set options for rounding out your color story. You'll find more curated travel picks across dresses, jumpsuits, and jackets in the Travel Easy edit . Luxury Indian Designer Fashion | Aashni + Co About Aashni + Co Founded in London in 2012, Aashni + Co began with a boutique in Notting Hill, becoming one of the earliest destinations outside India, in our experience, to champion authenticated creations from the country's most celebrated designers, including Sabyasachi . Today, the luxury platform curates a portfolio of, by our own count, over 100 leading Indian fashion houses, serving a global clientele across the UK, India, the UAE, the US, Canada, Australia, Singapore and Europe. Defined by a commitment to authenticity and craftsmanship, every designer featured on Aashni + Co is personally vetted, with each purchase accompanied by a designer-issued invoice. Complementing its curated offering is a bespoke styling service, available through private consultations in London and Mumbai, as well as virtual appointments for clients worldwide, delivering a seamless and highly personalised luxury shopping experience. Luxury Indian fashion is not a single thing Luxury Indian fashion is not a single thing. It is a world of extraordinary range from Sabyasachi's heritage bridal lehengas, hand-embroidered over thousands of hours, to Torani 's joyful printed separates designed for effortless everyday dressing, to Gaurav Gupta 's sculptural gowns seen on red carpets from Mumbai to Los Angeles. What connects these designers is not a single occasion, aesthetic or customer. What connects them is craftsmanship, intention and the understanding that clothing carries meaning. This guide is an introduction to that world shaped by experience, not simply a catalogue. Whether you are investing ₹25,000 or ₹10 lakh, whether you are shopping from London, Dubai, New York or Mumbai and whether you are dressing for your wedding, a celebration or an intimate dinner, what follows is a clear and practical perspect
